# Local FFmpeg H.264 VA-API profile-selection path

**AI disclosure:** This file, including its title and all prose, was generated by AI.

Offline implementation child of [driver #37](https://github.com/iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request/issues/37)
for [omarchy-m1-video#73](https://github.com/iconidentify/omarchy-m1-video/issues/73).
It turns the accepted #41 proposal into extracted callbacks plus a local
FFmpeg n9.0.1 patch. No installed FFmpeg, package pin, device or module
operation. AVC remains 73/135 through ordinary VA-API. Parent #37 stays open.

## Parser / callback order

FFmpeg n9.0.1 `ff_vaapi_decode_init` / `vaapi_decode_make_config` picks a VA
profile once from `avctx->profile`. Hardware buffers are created in
`vaapi_h264_start_frame` and `vaapi_h264_decode_slice`. `vaapi_h264_end_frame`
calls `ff_vaapi_decode_issue`. A later PPS/slice change is therefore checked
in start_frame and decode_slice **before** those VA calls. A rejected picture
sets a sticky flag, cancels, and end_frame does not issue. Already-issued
earlier pictures are not undone. This is an **explicit stop**, not software
fallback or reference-state replay.

The whole-inventory Python oracle under `experiments/h264-profile-selection/`
is not this live callback path. Fixture flags there remain synthetic.

## Run

```
python3 experiments/h264-client-selection/tests.py
python3 experiments/h264-client-selection/prepare.py /tmp/ffmpeg-n901-h264
```

`tests.py` builds the extracted callbacks (the same rules as the patch) with a
VA submit stub. Removing the FMO gate makes an FMO picture submit; that is the
required negative. `prepare.py` fetches the three hash-locked n9.0.1 files and
applies `ffmpeg-n9.0.1-h264-vaapi-select.patch` into a fresh directory. It does
not install FFmpeg. A full ARM64 FFmpeg link is optional and not required for
this leaf's hosted checks.

## Selection

Baseline without `constraint_set1` tentatively uses Constrained Baseline;
Extended uses Main. Ordinary Main/High/Constrained Baseline keep exact
matches. Reject FMO, fields/MBAFF, data-partition NALs 2–4, SP/SI, 4:2:0
mismatch and unequal/unsupported bit depth. No blanket `allow_profile_mismatch`.
High 10 stays conditional; this experiment does not query a device.
